paper_title: Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners A Comprehensive   Evaluation and Beyond
caption: The evaluation matches between LLM judge and human annotations on the 300 samples.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the evaluation matches between large language model (LLM) judges and human annotations across 300 samples, categorized by six distinct criteria: "Correct," "Rigorous," "Self-aware," "Active," "Oriented," and "No Hallucination." The horizontal axis represents the percentage scale from 0% to 100%, with tick marks at 20% intervals. The vertical axis lists the six evaluation categories in descending order of match percentage. Each bar is divided into two segments: a dark blue segment labeled "Matched" and a light blue segment labeled "Not Matched," as indicated by the legend. The "Matched" portion of each bar shows the percentage of agreement between LLM and human annotations, while the "Not Matched" portion shows the percentage of disagreement. For "Correct," the match rate is 99.0% with 1.00% not matched. For "Rigorous," it is 95.33% matched and 4.67% not matched. "Self-aware" shows 94.00% matched and 6.00% not matched. "Active" has 97.00% matched and 3.00% not matched. "Oriented" shows 97.33% matched and 2.67% not matched. Finally, "No Hallucination" has the highest match rate at 98.33% with 1.67% not matched. The bars are sorted in descending order of match percentage, with "Correct" at the top and "Self-aware" at the bottom. All bars are horizontally oriented, and the chart uses a clean, minimal design with no additional annotations or visual emphasis.
